quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle if the line between your lane and the lane you want to enter is a ____ line.
questions.correctAnswerText: Broken white
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes going in the same direction. You can cross broken white lines to pass if the passing lane is clear.

questions.question: Highway signs that tell drivers about dangerous conditions are called:
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning signs.
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to possible dangers. Ignoring warning signs can cause accidents.

questions.question: You are driving on a one-way street. You can only turn left onto another one-way street if:

options.text: Traffic on that street moves to the right.
Traffic on that street moves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic on that street moves to the left.
questions.explanation: You can turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves to the left, if there is no sign stopping you. You cannot turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves to the right.

questions.question: When double solid yellow lines separate traffic lanes:

options.text: You can pass from the left.
You can pass from the right.
You cannot pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mean traffic is moving in opposite directions. Double solid yellow lines mean no passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.question: This is a ____ sign.
questions.correctAnswerText: Yield
questions.explanation: This triangular sign is a "Yield" sign. Slow down and check for traffic. Let pedestrians and oncoming traffic go first. Stop only if needed.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly is not unsafe.
Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly can be dangerous because drivers behind you may get frustrated and pass unsafely. Drive with traffic flow, within the legal speed limit.

questions.question: While driving on a road with a single broken white line in the middle:

options.text: You must stay in your lane.
You can cross the line to change lanes.
You can change lanes only from the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can cross the line to change lanes.
questions.explanation: White lines mean lanes go in the same direction. Broken white lines mean you can pass another vehicle when it is safe.

questions.question: When dealing with pedestrians, a driver must:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always give pedestrians the right-of-way, even if they are wrong.
Give the right-of-way only when the pedestrian has it by law.
Slow down and honk near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always give pedestrians the right-of-way, even if they are wrong.
questions.explanation: Do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian or vehicle, no matter what. It is your job as a driver to watch for pedestrians and let them cross safely, even if they are crossing illegally.

questions.question: Excessive speed:

options.text: Helps you react to dangers faster.
Often leads to risky driving choices.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often leads to risky driving choices.
questions.explanation: Excessive speed is a major cause of crashes. It does not save time and often leads to risky driving choices.

questions.question: At dusk or on cloudy days, you should:

options.text: Drive with your four-way flashers on.
Drive with your parking lights on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: At dusk or on cloudy days, turn on your headlights. Use low beams when within 1,000 feet of oncoming vehicles and within 500 feet of vehicles ahead. Always use low beams in poor weather.

questions.question: It is illegal for a person 21 years of age or older to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:
questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent.
questions.explanation: For drivers 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Drinking and driving is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Worn or bald tires:
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires increase stopping distance and make turning harder. They also increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: You are driving on the freeway behind a large truck. You should drive:

options.text: Closely behind the truck in bad weather because the driver can see farther ahead than you can.
Farther behind the truck than you would behind a passenger vehicle.
No more than one car length behind the truck so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther behind the truck than you would behind a passenger vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely behind a truck, the driver cannot see you in the side mirrors. Tailgating is dangerous because you lose your safety distance if the truck stops suddenly.

questions.question: You may drive around the gates at a railroad crossing:

options.text: When the lights have stopped flashing.
When other drivers drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under no circumstances.
questions.explanation: You must stop at all railroad crossings when warning signals appear. These signals include flashing red lights, lowered gates, a flagger, or train sounds. Never drive around a lowered gate.

questions.question: When driving on snow or ice:

options.text: It is safe to use your cruise control.
Make speed and directional changes more slowly than you normally would.
Drive as you would under normal conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make speed and directional changes more slowly than you normally would.
questions.explanation: On snow or ice, make all speed and direction changes slowly. Never use cruise control on snow or ice because your tires may lose grip and you could lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: When rain or fog reduces visibility, drivers should use their:
questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain, snow, sleet, or fog. High beams reflect off precipitation and shine back into your eyes, reducing visibility.

questions.question: Collisions are more likely to happen when:

options.text: All vehicles are traveling at about the same speed.
One lane of traffic is traveling faster than other lanes.
One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than other traffic.
questions.explanation: Collisions happen more often when one driver goes faster or slower than other traffic. Speeding increases crash risk. Driving too slowly also causes crashes and makes other drivers swerve to avoid you.

questions.question: Highway pavement is most slippery:

options.text: If it has been raining for several hours.
If it has just begun to rain.
If it has been raining for one to two hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: If it has just begun to rain.
questions.explanation: Pavement is slipperiest when rain first starts. Dirt and oil on the road mix with water, creating a greasy coating.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that a divided highway begins ahead. The road splits into two separate one-way roads. You must stay to the right.

questions.question: The most common cause of motorcycle accidents is:

options.text: A car driver failing to yield and turning left in front of an oncoming motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: A car driver failing to yield and turning left in front of an oncoming motorcycle.
questions.explanation: About one-third of motorcycle crashes involve another vehicle. Many happen when a car driver turns left in front of an oncoming motorcycle without properly yielding the right-of-way.

questions.question: When entering the interstate, find a gap in traffic, match the speed of other cars, signal, and:

options.text: Expect other drivers to let you in because you have the right-of-way.
Wait until the lane is completely clear before merging.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge safely into the gap.
questions.explanation: Find a gap in traffic, speed up to match other cars, and signal before merging. Merge into the gap when it is safe. Watch for other traffic and do not count on other drivers to make room for you.

questions.question: If you drive slower than the traffic around you, you will most likely:

options.text: Block traffic and get a ticket.

questions.correctAnswerText: Block traffic and get a ticket.
questions.explanation: You must drive slowly during heavy traffic or bad weather. However, driving too slowly and blocking traffic flow can result in a ticket. Match the speed of traffic unless it is above the legal speed limit.

questions.question: This yellow sign means:

options.text: A sharp right turn is ahead.
You can only turn right on a green arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: A sharp right turn is ahead.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have a bright yellow-green background. They warn you about upcoming road conditions like curves and sharp turns.

questions.question: By driving on Nebraska roads, you agree to take a chemical test if a police officer asks you to.
questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Nebraska has an Implied Consent Law. By driving in the state, you automatically agree to take a chemical test if a police officer asks you to.

questions.question: It is against the law to drive next to a motorcycle in the same lane.
questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Never share a lane with a motorcycle, even if there seems to be enough room. Motorcycles need the full lane width to move safely.
